faqs.q: When can bats be removed from a Charlottesville attic?
faqs.a: Bats in Virginia are handled by exclusion only — one-way exits fitted and every other opening sealed so the colony leaves on its own. Under our permit conditions the maternity season runs May 1 through August 15, and bats may not be excluded or removed then unless no young are present or there is a threat to human health or safety, so we inspect any time but schedule most Charlottesville exclusions outside that window. Since January 1, 2025, bat work also requires a CNAP holder with DWR-recognized bat training, which is how our crew works.

Charlottesville.wildlife_intro:
Charlottesville is a compact university city surrounded by Albemarle County — its older neighborhoods are bat and raccoon country in Charlottesville. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: rivanna River, Downtown Mall, University of Virginia grounds and foothill neighborhoods. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Charlottesville — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
